stops.note: 'paved road', strata from sternere 'to lay down'; Roman engineers built some 80,000 km of paved highways
Anglo-Saxons called the Roman roads they inherited 'streets', as in Watling Street and Ermine Street
shifted from 'highway' to a road lined with houses; medieval London's Fleet Street took its name from the River Fleet it crossed

current_meaning: a public road in a city or town, usually with buildings along it
